tables.name: users
tables.purpose: One row per person who holds an account — customer, manager or admin; the identity every booking, audit row and reset token points at.
tables.cite: P-ACC-01 (E5 S4, 'The complete field list of the user row') · E8 S7.5 · FR-ADR-050

columns.name: id
columns.cite: P-ACC-09 — 'booking.user_id integer NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT'; EP-ADM-22/EP-ADM-23 return user_id as 'integer'; P-XCT-03's worked example uses actor_user_id 17
columns.note: INTEGER, not uuid. Three documents spell the referencing column `integer`, so the brief's uuid default does not apply here. NO DOCUMENT STATES THE GENERATION MECHANISM (identity column vs sequence) — audit_log is the only table where a document says 'identity'.

columns.name: email
columns.cite: P-ACC-01 step 5 and its validation table · E8 S7.5 · P-XCT-06 preconditions
columns.note: Stored AS ENTERED, 3..254 characters after trimming. Uniqueness is a unique index on `lower(email)` — E8 S7.5 explicitly refuses a second lowercased column ('two fields to keep in step'), so this is NOT citext and NOT a stored lowercase column. Written once by P-ACC-01 and never updated by anything (S-ACC-06 asserts the mapper's changed-attribute set never contains `email`).

columns.name: password_hash
columns.cite: P-ACC-01 (field table: `text`, NOT NULL) · P-ACC-03 (bcrypt, BCRYPT_COST default 12) · S-ACC-02
columns.note: bcrypt. The ALGORITHM IS NAMED BY THE DOCUMENTS (P-ACC-03: 'Algorithm bcrypt'; E8 S7.5; FR-ADR-050) — nothing is inferred. NOT NULL on every row without exception: a manager account with no usable password carries a real bcrypt digest of 32 discarded CSPRNG bytes, drawn PER ROW so two such rows never share a value (S-ACC-02 asserts count(*) - count(DISTINCT password_hash) = 0 over rows with last_signed_in_at IS NULL). A nullable column is refused by name, because a null test before the verification is the early return P-ACC-03's timing property forbids.

columns.name: role
columns.cite: S3.1 'The four roles' (Modelled as: `user.role = 'customer'` / `'manager'` / `'admin'`) · P-XCT-05 preconditions ('exactly one role value in a single column') · FR-ADR-009 · SRC-003 C-1
columns.note: PROVISIONAL that the manager value exists at all (SRC-003 C-1). Roles are mutually exclusive, one column, never a many-to-many table (S3.1, FR-ADR-050). Set to 'customer' by the application at registration and to 'manager' by P-ADM-17; NO ENDPOINT EVER CREATES 'admin' (S-ADM-18 asserts every /api/admin POST and PUT leaves the admin count unchanged and that `role = 'admin'` appears only in scripts/seed.py). NO DOCUMENT STATES THE DATABASE REPRESENTATION — see gaps.

columns.name: password_version
columns.cite: P-ACC-05 ('an integer starting at 1 and incremented on every password change') · P-ACC-01 step 5 · P-ACC-08 step 4
columns.note: THE SESSION-INVALIDATION COUNTER. It is the JWT's `pv` claim; the authorisation dependency loads the user row by primary key on every authenticated request and rejects the token when `pv` does not match this column (P-ACC-05 exception 4). Written as 1 by the application at insert — no document states a database default. Incremented by P-ACC-08 only: `password_version = password_version + 1`.

columns.name: created_at
columns.cite: P-ACC-01 step 5 · FR-ADR-018 ('`created_at` and `updated_at` are `timestamptz` and default to `now()` at the database') · EP-ADM-22 returns it
columns.note: Required on every table in the schema — S-XCT-09 asserts that no table in `public` other than `alembic_version` lacks a `created_at`.

columns.name: last_signed_in_at
columns.cite: P-ACC-01 (field table: timestamptz, UTC, nullable) · P-ACC-02 step 4 · P-ACC-08 step 4
columns.note: NULL means the account has never signed in — a real and expected state, not a defect. Written from the INJECTED CLOCK on every successful sign-in (`UPDATE users SET last_signed_in_at = :now WHERE id = :id`) and inside P-ACC-08's reset transaction. NOT written on a failed attempt. `has_signed_in` on EP-ADM-22 is DERIVED as `last_signed_in_at IS NOT NULL` and is never stored (S-ADM-18 asserts no `has_signed_in` column exists in information_schema).

unique.cite: P-ACC-01 step 3 · P-XCT-06 preconditions ('A unique index exists on `lower(email)`') · E8 S7.5
unique.why: Email is the identity, unique case-insensitively. It is an EXPRESSION index, not a column constraint — a second lowercased column is refused by name in S7.5. It is the guard, not a prior read: P-ACC-01 step 6 catches the unique violation and translates it to 409 EMAIL_ALREADY_REGISTERED, and S-ACC-01 asserts 20 simultaneous identical registrations produce exactly 1 success and 19 conflicts with no 500.

indexes.why: Every sign-in and every reset request loads the row by `lower(email)`; registration checks it. Same object as the unique constraint above.

tables.name: password_reset_token
tables.purpose: One row per password-reset request: the SHA-256 of a token that is never stored, its expiry, whether it was spent, and the two separate columns that track the worker's send of the reset email.
tables.cite: P-ACC-07 step 5 and its two-column table · P-ACC-08 step 4 · E4 P-TKT-12

columns.name: id
columns.cite: P-TKT-12 server-side validation — '`reset_token_id`: integer, positive, existing' · S-TKT-15 (`WHERE id=:t`)
columns.note: The queue message carries this id and NEVER the token. No document states the generation mechanism.

columns.name: user_id
columns.cite: P-ACC-07 step 5 ('a `password_reset_token` row holding `user_id` ...') · S-ACC-07 (`WHERE user_id=:id`)
columns.note: The account the link is for. P-TKT-12 validates that the message's `user_id` matches this column; a mismatch is dead-lettered, never sent.

columns.name: token_sha256
columns.cite: P-ACC-07 step 5 ('`token_sha256` (the SHA-256 of the token, hex)') · S-ACC-07
columns.note: SHA-256 hex of a 43-character URL-safe token drawn from 32 CSPRNG bytes. ONLY THE HASH IS STORED — 'somebody who can read the table cannot mint a session from it'. P-ACC-08 step 1 looks the row up by this value. S-ACC-07 asserts the 43 characters appear in `SELECT password_reset_token::text`, in the 202 body and in DEBUG-level stdout NOWHERE. DO NOT ADD A PLAINTEXT TOKEN COLUMN — see gaps, OPEN-RESETTOKEN-01.

columns.name: expires_at
columns.cite: P-ACC-07 step 5 and its worked example ('`expires_at = created_at + PASSWORD_RESET_TTL_SECONDS`')
columns.note: PASSWORD_RESET_TTL_SECONDS default 1800 (a [JUDGMENT CALL], configuration, not a ruled number). Compared against the INJECTED clock in UTC (FR-ADR-018). The 1800 must not appear as a literal in a constraint or a message — every customer-visible '30 minutes' is rendered from the variable.

columns.name: used_at
columns.cite: P-ACC-07 step 5 · P-ACC-08 step 4 · S-SCP-04 ('The password_reset_token.used_at column is explicitly excluded from the check and must still exist')
columns.note: THE THIRD AND SEPARATE TIMESTAMP: it records the CUSTOMER SPENDING the token and has nothing to do with the send. The single-use guarantee is the conditional update `UPDATE password_reset_token SET used_at = :now WHERE id = :id AND used_at IS NULL` affecting exactly one row inside the password-change transaction — not a prior read. P-ACC-07 step 3 also sets it on every outstanding unused token for that user, so at most one live token exists per account. NOTE THE NEAR-MISS: S-SCP-04's excluded-column sweep bans `used_at` on `booking` and MUST NOT trip over this column.

columns.name: email_claimed_at
columns.cite: P-ACC-07 step 5 and its column table ('a worker is holding this send job') · E4 P-TKT-12 step 2 and exceptions 3a, 4, 6
columns.note: A CLAIM, NOT A RECORD OF DELIVERY. Set by the conditional claim; CLEARED BACK TO NULL on an SES refusal or a SES_SEND_TIMEOUT_MS timeout (`UPDATE password_reset_token SET email_claimed_at = NULL WHERE id = :id AND email_sent_at IS NULL`); and overtaken by the age branch `email_claimed_at < now() - :stale_interval` (RECEIPT_CLAIM_STALE_SECONDS, 900) when a worker dies before it can clear anything. These are ONE reclaim mechanism with a fast path, not two.

columns.name: email_sent_at
columns.cite: P-ACC-07 step 5 and its column table ('an email went out … never cleared by anything') · E4 P-TKT-12 step 4 and exception 3
columns.note: TERMINAL. Set only after SES accepts, and NEVER CLEARED BY ANYTHING — that is what makes a duplicate credential email impossible even if the queue delete fails and SQS redelivers a day later (S-TKT-15 asserts a redelivery 24 injected hours later makes 0 SES calls).

columns.name: created_at
columns.cite: P-ACC-07 step 5 (the row holds `created_at`) · FR-ADR-018 · S-XCT-09 (every table carries created_at)
columns.note: See gaps: S-ACC-07 asserts `expires_at = created_at + 1800 seconds FROM THE INJECTED CLOCK`, which a database-side `now()` default cannot satisfy under an injected test clock.

foreign_keys.cite: S-XCT-09 — `SELECT conname, confdeltype FROM pg_constraint WHERE contype = 'f' AND confdeltype <> 'r'` returns 0 ROWS, i.e. EVERY foreign key in the schema is RESTRICT · P-XCT-04 · FR-ADR-012

indexes.cite: P-ACC-08 step 1 ('hashes the submitted token with SHA-256 and looks the row up by that hash') · P-ACC-08's rate-limit rationale ('it bounds the indexed lookup per guess')
indexes.why: The confirm endpoint's only lookup. DERIVED FROM THE NAMED QUERY — no document declares this index, and no document says whether it is unique (see gaps).

indexes.cite: P-ACC-07 step 3 ('marks every outstanding unused reset token for that user as used') · S-ACC-07 (`SELECT count(*) FROM password_reset_token WHERE user_id=:id AND used_at IS NULL`)
indexes.why: The per-user sweep that keeps at most one live token per account. DERIVED FROM THE NAMED QUERY, not declared by any document.

tables.name: audit_log
tables.purpose: One append-only row per privileged write, inserted in the same database transaction as the change itself, recording who, when, which action, which row, and the changed fields before and after.

columns.name: id
columns.cite: E8 S7.3 and P-ADM-19 and FR-ADR-019 all spell it '`bigint` identity' · P-RPT-11 step 3 (cursor on `id`, ordered descending)
columns.note: THE ONLY PRIMARY KEY IN THIS CLUSTER A DOCUMENT GIVES A GENERATION MECHANISM FOR. EP-RPT-04's `cursor` is a positive integer audit row id and is a BOUND, not a lookup: a well-formed id naming no row returns 200, never 404.

columns.name: occurred_at
columns.cite: E8 S7.3 · P-ADM-19 · S-XCT-06 (`SELECT data_type ... column_name='occurred_at'` returns 'timestamp with time zone')
columns.note: UTC. S-XCT-06 additionally asserts the value the APPLICATION BINDS is an aware datetime whose utcoffset() is zero — so it is written by the application from the injected clock, not by a database default.

columns.name: actor_user_id
columns.cite: E8 S7.3 · P-ADM-19 · P-XCT-03 server-side validation · S-XCT-06 (`is_nullable` returns NO, and one foreign key row in pg_constraint)
columns.note: NEVER A ROLE NAME AND NEVER A SERVICE ACCOUNT — both substitutes are forbidden in terms. The seed script is the ONLY exemption from the same-transaction audit rule anywhere in the product, precisely because at its earliest writes no user row exists to point at (P-XCT-30); it writes zero audit rows and no application code path inherits that exemption.

columns.name: actor_role
columns.cite: E8 S7.3 · P-ADM-19 · S-XCT-06 (asserted still to read 'admin' after user 17's role is changed to manager)
columns.note: THE ROLE THE ACTOR HELD AT THE TIME, COPIED RATHER THAN JOINED. Never resolved by a join at read time. NO DOCUMENT STATES THE COLUMN TYPE — `text` is reported rather than `enum:user_role` because the point of the column is that it is a frozen copy, and a shared enum type ties historical rows to a live vocabulary. See gaps; this is the merge owner's call.

columns.name: action
columns.cite: E8 S7.3 · P-ADM-19's controlled vocabulary table (the single source of the strings for the whole product) · FR-ADR-019
columns.note: A CLOSED controlled vocabulary, enumerated by P-ADM-19 and by no one else. ENFORCED IN THE APPLICATION, NOT IN THE DATABASE: S-ADM-02 requires a closed Python enum `AuditAction`, S-XCT-07 requires a module-level tuple `AUDIT_ACTIONS` in backend/app/domain/audit.py, and a non-member is refused at a boundary check BEFORE THE TRANSACTION OPENS (asserted by a statement listener recording zero statements). No document asks for a database CHECK or a Postgres enum, so none is proposed. The string already got wrong once: a base-price change is `showtime.base_price_changed`; `showtime.price_changed` is NOT a member and never has been, although FR-ADR-019's own example text still shows it.

columns.name: entity_type
columns.cite: E8 S7.3 · P-ADM-19
columns.note: The table the change landed on. Values seen in the vocabulary table: movie, showtime, seat_category, cinema, screen, seat, user, manager_screen_assignment, language, certification, genre, format.

columns.name: entity_id
columns.cite: E8 S7.3 · P-ADM-19
columns.note: The primary key of the changed row. NO FOREIGN KEY MAY EXIST ON THIS COLUMN — S-ADM-18 asserts the FK count on audit_log.entity_id is 0, because for `manager.screen_unassigned` it deliberately names a row that no longer exists and 'a column that resolves by lying about what it points at is worse than one that honestly points at something gone'. Nothing may join it to a live table for that action. Width is not stated by any document — see gaps.

columns.name: before
columns.cite: E8 S7.3 · P-ADM-19 · P-XCT-03 server-side validation
columns.note: ONLY THE FIELDS THAT CHANGED, never a whole-row snapshot (S-XCT-06 asserts jsonb_object_keys(before) counts 1 for a single-field change). NULL FOR A CREATION. Carries no credential (`password_hash`, `password_version` excluded from every entity_type='user' row), no card-shaped key, and no poster bytes — only the S3 object key.

columns.name: after
columns.cite: E8 S7.3 · P-ADM-19
columns.note: Null for a withdrawal that changes nothing else — including `manager.screen_unassigned`, whose `before` carries exactly `{"user_id": n, "screen_id": n}`. Same credential and card-data exclusions as `before`. Returned VERBATIM by EP-RPT-04 and never unit-converted.

columns.name: request_id
columns.cite: E8 S7.3 · P-ADM-19 · P-XCT-03 happy path step 4 and preconditions · FR-ADR-056
columns.note: The request id from the log context, so an audit row joins to the log lines. Matches ^[0-9a-f]{8}$ (S-XCT-06). NO DOCUMENT STATES ITS NULLABILITY EXPLICITLY — reported NOT NULL because P-XCT-03's precondition requires it to be available before the transaction opens and every audit row is written from a request; flag it if the merge disagrees.

foreign_keys.cite: P-XCT-03 ('non-null foreign key to the acting user') · S-XCT-06 (one pg_constraint FK row on audit_log) · S-XCT-09 (every FK in the schema is confdeltype 'r')

indexes.cite: P-RPT-11 happy path step 2 (a half-open UTC window from `from`/`to`) and step 4 (`available_actions` and `available_actors` computed over the same window)
indexes.why: Every read of this table is bounded by the date window, deliberately, because audit_log is the largest table in the system and never shrinks. DERIVED FROM THE NAMED QUERY — no document declares an index on this table.

tables.name: manager_screen_assignment
tables.purpose: One row per (manager user, screen) pair — the whole of manager scope; the router dependency resolves the caller's screen ids from it and every manager query filters on that set.
tables.cite: FR-ADR-011 (APPROVED) · P-ADM-17 · E8 S7.5 · S3.1 · P-XCT-05 preconditions

columns.name: id
columns.cite: P-ADM-19 ('For `manager.screen_unassigned` it is the primary key the removed `manager_screen_assignment` row had') · S-ADM-18 (`SELECT count(*) FROM manager_screen_assignment WHERE id = :that_entity_id` returns 0)
columns.note: A surrogate key is required because the audit row records the id the deleted row held. Generation mechanism not stated.

columns.name: user_id
columns.cite: FR-ADR-011 ('one row per (manager user, screen)') · S-ADM-18 (`(user_id, screen_id)` unique, asserted by name in information_schema) · P-ADM-19 (`before` carries exactly the keys user_id and screen_id)
columns.note: Must reference an account whose role is `manager`: EP-ADM-24 returns 422 'That account is not a manager account. Screens can only be assigned to managers.' That check is application-side; no document asks for a database constraint on it.

columns.name: screen_id
columns.cite: FR-ADR-011 · EP-ADM-23/EP-ADM-24 (`screen_ids`: array of integer) · S-ADM-18
columns.note: OWNED JOINTLY WITH THE VENUE CLUSTER — the referenced table is `screen`.

columns.name: created_at
columns.cite: S-XCT-09 — no table in `public` other than `alembic_version` may lack a `created_at` · FR-ADR-018
columns.note: Required by the schema-wide rule rather than by a row that names this column. Flagged so the merge owner can see the derivation.

unique.cite: FR-ADR-011 ('unique on the pair') · P-ADM-17 · S-ADM-18 ('(user_id, screen_id) is unique on manager_screen_assignment, asserted by name in information_schema')
unique.why: One assignment per manager per hall. EP-ADM-24 replaces the complete set and rejects a duplicate screen_id in the request body with 422 before it reaches the constraint.

foreign_keys.cite: S-XCT-09 (every FK in the schema is confdeltype 'r') · FR-ADR-012
S-XCT-09 (every FK in the schema is confdeltype 'r') · FR-ADR-012

indexes.cite: P-XCT-05 step 3 · EP-RPT-01's authorisation_rule ('manager means the set from manager_screen_assignment, possibly empty')
indexes.why: Resolved once per manager request by the router dependency. DERIVED FROM THE NAMED QUERY; the unique index above already leads on user_id, so this may be redundant — the merge owner should collapse it.

enums.name: user_role
enums.cite: S3.1 'The four roles' — guest is 'the absence of a session; not a row' · P-XCT-05 · FR-ADR-009 · SRC-003 C-1 (PROVISIONAL)
enums.note: THREE VALUES IN THE DATABASE, FOUR ROLES IN THE PRODUCT. S3.1's 'Modelled as' column gives a `user.role` value for customer, manager and admin only, and models guest as the absence of a session. Meanwhile S-SCP-06 asserts the APPLICATION's `Role` enum has exactly four members — sorted values ['admin','customer','guest','manager'] and len(Role) == 4. Those two are consistent only if the application enum and the database column are different things: guest is an authorisation outcome, not a stored value. NO DOCUMENT SAYS WHETHER THIS IS A POSTGRES ENUM TYPE OR text — see gaps. There is NO cinema-staff, usher, door or scanner value: SRC-001 §4.3 is withdrawn by erratum E-1 and S-SCP-06 asserts no member name matches staff|usher|door|gate|scanner|attendant.

gaps.what: OPEN-RESETTOKEN-01 — the password-reset flow as specified cannot be built. Three passages are jointly unsatisfiable: P-ACC-07 step 4 says the token itself is never stored (the row keeps only `token_sha256`); E4 P-TKT-12 says the token never travels in the queue (the payload key set is exactly message_version, request_id, reset_token_id, user_id); and P-TKT-12 step 3 requires the worker to render an email whose link is `{PUBLIC_BASE_URL}/account/reset/confirm?token=<token>`. Nothing downstream holds the 43 characters.
gaps.why_it_matters: Every resolution breaks one of the three rules — a plaintext column defeats the hash, a token in the payload sends a credential through a queue at rest, rendering the link at enqueue time sends it through the queue inside the link. Which rule gives is a decision about how a credential is handled. NO PLAINTEXT TOKEN COLUMN IS MODELLED HERE AND NONE IS PROPOSED. It blocks a working feature, not a document, and Phase 2 reaches it: the seeded manager accounts' only specified route to a usable password is this flow (P-XCT-32, P-ADM-17 step 4).
gaps.where_you_looked: CONSTITUTION.md Article X.0f row OPEN-RESETTOKEN-01 · E5 P-ACC-07 steps 4-6 · E4 P-TKT-12 preconditions and step 3 · Bible S-ACC-07's own escalation note

gaps.what: audit_log has no `created_at`, but S-XCT-09 asserts that NO table in `public` other than `alembic_version` lacks one.
gaps.why_it_matters: That acceptance criterion is a query that will run: `SELECT table_name FROM information_schema.tables t WHERE table_schema = 'public' AND table_name <> 'alembic_version' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.columns c WHERE c.table_name = t.table_name AND c.column_name = 'created_at')` must return 0 rows. audit_log's ten columns as published by FR-ADR-019, E8 S7.3 and P-ADM-19 are id, occurred_at, actor_user_id, actor_role, action, entity_type, entity_id, before, after, request_id — `occurred_at` is the instant column and it is not called `created_at`. Either the criterion needs an exemption for audit_log, or audit_log gains an eleventh column no specification asks for. I have NOT added one.
gaps.where_you_looked: Bible S-XCT-09 AcceptanceCriteria · E8 S7.3 column table · P-ADM-19 column table · FR-ADR-019 column table

gaps.what: The database representation of `role` is unspecified: Postgres enum type, text with a CHECK, or bare text.
gaps.why_it_matters: Every document states only that 'the user row carries exactly one role value in a single column'. S-ADM-18 and S-XCT-46 compare it to string literals (`WHERE role = 'admin'`), which works under all three. I report `enum:user_role` so the six cluster outputs merge on one name, but the choice is the merge owner's and it is not derived from a citation. A native enum also interacts with the PROVISIONAL role set: if the client reverses SRC-003 C-1 to three roles, removing the `manager` value from a native enum is harder than removing it from a CHECK.
gaps.where_you_looked: S3.1 · P-XCT-05 preconditions · E8 S7.5 · FR-ADR-009 · FR-ADR-050 · Bible S-SCP-06, S-ADM-18

gaps.what: `guest` is in the application Role enum (S-SCP-06 asserts len(Role) == 4 including 'guest') but is not a value any user row can hold (S3.1: 'the absence of a session; not a row').
gaps.why_it_matters: If the merge owner creates a native `user_role` type with four values, a guest row becomes representable — a row that can never sign in and that every authorisation dependency would have to branch on. If they create it with three, the application enum and the database type share a name and disagree on membership, which is how a later developer 'fixes' one of them. The documents support three values in the column and four in the code; naming the database type something other than the application enum would remove the trap, and no document forbids that.
gaps.where_you_looked: S3.1 'The four roles' table, Modelled-as column · Bible S-SCP-06 · P-XCT-05's role table · FR-ADR-009

gaps.what: The type and width of `audit_log.actor_role` and `audit_log.entity_id` are stated by no document.
gaps.why_it_matters: `actor_role` is a frozen copy of a role, so binding it to a live enum type would let a vocabulary change rewrite what a historical row means — the exact thing 'copied rather than joined' exists to prevent. `entity_id` must be at least as wide as the widest primary key in the finished schema, and it must carry NO foreign key (S-ADM-18 asserts the FK count on it is 0). Both are merge-owner decisions and both are reported here rather than guessed at.
gaps.where_you_looked: E8 S7.3 · P-ADM-19 · FR-ADR-019 · Bible S-XCT-06, S-ADM-18

gaps.what: Bible S-ACC-03 contains `SELECT count(*) FROM audit_log WHERE user_id=:id returns 0`. audit_log has no `user_id` column — the column is `actor_user_id`.
gaps.why_it_matters: THIS SQL WILL BE RUN AS A TEST AND WILL RAISE UndefinedColumn, not return 0. The intent (signing in writes no audit row) is correct and is stated in prose by P-ACC-02 and P-ADM-17; only the column name is wrong. Adding a `user_id` column to audit_log to satisfy it would be a schema defect. The criterion should read `WHERE actor_user_id = :id`.
gaps.where_you_looked: docs/05 Bible/FrontRow_Bible.csv row S-ACC-03 · E8 S7.3 · P-ADM-19

gaps.what: The Bible uses two names for the users table. S-ACC-01 and S-ACC-03 assert against `information_schema.columns ... table_name='users'`; S-SCP-04 asserts 'the same query against table_name='user''; S-ADM-02 and S-ADM-18 say 'the user table' and 'The user row has exactly seven fields'.
gaps.why_it_matters: The goal contract fixes the name as `users`, so S-SCP-04's `table_name='user'` sweep will match zero rows and pass VACUOUSLY — it would never catch a loyalty/tier/points column if one were added. It is a silent test, not a failing one, which is worse.
gaps.where_you_looked: Bible S-ACC-01, S-ACC-03, S-SCP-04, S-ADM-02, S-ADM-18 · the GOAL_08 brief's fixed table list

gaps.what: `password_reset_token.created_at` cannot simultaneously default to the database clock and satisfy S-ACC-07's assertion that `expires_at = created_at + 1800 seconds from the injected clock`.
gaps.why_it_matters: FR-ADR-018 rules that `created_at` and `updated_at` default to `now()` at the database and that 'the injected clock governs domain decisions; the database clock governs row metadata'. But `expires_at` IS a domain decision derived from `created_at`, and S-ACC-07 asserts 'a token created at 10:00:00Z has expires_at 10:30:00Z' against an injected clock. Under a database default the two instants come from two clocks and a test that advances the injected clock will see them disagree. Either the application binds `created_at` on this table, or `expires_at` is computed from the injected instant independently and the assertion is rewritten. I have reported the default FR-ADR-018 states and flagged the conflict rather than picking one.
gaps.where_you_looked: FR-ADR-018 lines 101-102 · P-ACC-07 step 5 and its worked example · Bible S-ACC-07

gaps.what: E4 P-TKT-12's published claim SQL uses the DATABASE clock — `AND (email_claimed_at IS NULL OR email_claimed_at < now() - :stale_interval)` — while S-TKT-15 requires the staleness threshold to be bound from the same INJECTED clock that wrote `email_claimed_at`.
gaps.why_it_matters: S-TKT-15 asserts a redelivery at claim + 120 injected seconds makes 0 SES calls and one at claim + 901 injected seconds reclaims the row. A `now()` in the WHERE clause reads the container's clock and the injected-time test cannot move it, so the criterion cannot pass against the SQL as written. Art IX.5 also makes a test that reads the wall clock a defect. This bears directly on `email_claimed_at`, which is my column, so it is reported here; the fix belongs to E4.
gaps.where_you_looked: E4 P-TKT-12 step 2 SQL block · Bible S-TKT-15 · FR-ADR-018 · CLAUDE.md 'A test that reads the wall clock is a defect'

gaps.what: `users` carries no `updated_at`, although `password_hash`, `password_version` and `last_signed_in_at` are all mutated after creation.
gaps.why_it_matters: P-XCT-04's preconditions say 'tables that mutate carry `updated_at`' and S-XCT-09 repeats it as an implementer note. But P-ACC-01 states the complete field list as SEVEN columns and 'Nothing else', and S-ACC-01 and S-ACC-03 both assert `information_schema.columns` returns EXACTLY those seven. The explicit seven-column assertion wins and I have not added `updated_at`; the general rule is inconsistent with it and someone should say which governs.
gaps.where_you_looked: P-ACC-01 · P-XCT-04 preconditions · Bible S-ACC-01, S-ACC-03, S-XCT-09

gaps.what: `manager_screen_assignment` is required by an APPROVED ADR and by four Bible stories, but it is ABSENT from the GOAL_08 brief's fixed table list.
gaps.why_it_matters: Manager scope has nowhere else to live: FR-ADR-011 explicitly rejects a `screen_id` column on the user row, and S3.1 models the manager role as `user.role = 'manager'` PLUS this table. Without it P-XCT-05 step 3, EP-RPT-01's authorisation rule, EP-ADM-22/23/24 and the audit actions `manager.screen_assigned` / `manager.screen_unassigned` have no referent. I have modelled it in this cluster because it is (manager user, screen) and its primary axis is identity — but `screen_id` belongs to the venue cluster, so THE MERGE OWNER MUST DEDUPLICATE if the venue reader modelled it too.
gaps.where_you_looked: FR-ADR-011 Decision · P-ADM-17 · S3.1 · E8 S7.5 · Bible S-ADM-18, S-ADM-19, S-XCT-09, S-RPT-04 · the GOAL_08 brief's fixed table list

gaps.what: No document states whether `password_reset_token.token_sha256` is unique, nor whether any of the four primary keys in this cluster are identity columns, sequences or application-generated. Only `audit_log.id` is given a mechanism ('bigint identity').
gaps.why_it_matters: The brief's default (uuid, application-generated) does not hold here — every referencing column the documents spell is `integer` and every worked example uses small integers. A collision on `token_sha256` is a 2^-256 event so uniqueness is not a correctness guard, but the merge owner should decide it deliberately rather than by omission.

gaps.what: OPEN-EMAILOWN-01 and OPEN-MGRBOOK-01 both land on this cluster and neither changes a column.
gaps.why_it_matters: OPEN-EMAILOWN-01 (reserved: product) is the consequence that whoever controls a registered address controls the account, by the exact chain these columns implement — reset writes `password_hash`, increments `password_version`, and `pv` kills every live session. No endpoint patches `users.email` (S-ACC-06 asserts the mapper's changed-attribute set is exactly {last_signed_in_at, password_hash, password_version}), so THE SCHEMA IS ALREADY THE SHAPE THE RULING WILL NEED and no address-change column may be invented to soften it. OPEN-MGRBOOK-01 (reserved: access control) asks whether a manager may buy a ticket in a hall they report on — it is answered by authorisation, not by a column, and nothing here narrows or widens it.

notes: PRIMARY KEYS IN THIS CLUSTER ARE INTEGERS, NOT UUIDs, AND THE DOCUMENTS SAY SO EXPLICITLY. P-ACC-09 spells `booking.user_id integer NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT`; EP-ADM-22/23/24 declare `user_id` as integer; EP-RPT-04's cursor is 'integer, positive, an audit row id'; P-TKT-12 validates `reset_token_id` as 'integer, positive'. Only audit_log.id is given a width and a mechanism — 'bigint identity'. If another cluster reports uuid keys the two will not merge.

THE THREE TIMESTAMPS ON password_reset_token ARE THREE DIFFERENT FACTS AND COLLAPSING ANY PAIR IS A NAMED DEFECT. `email_claimed_at` = a worker holds this job, CLEARED on failure so the age branch can reclaim a dead worker's row. `email_sent_at` = an email actually went out, NEVER cleared by anything. `used_at` = the customer spent the token, unrelated to sending. P-TKT-12 records the exact regression that was already shipped once: the published claim SQL used `email_sent_at IS NULL` as the claim, so a worker that died between claim and send left `email_sent_at` set with nothing sent, every redelivery read 'already sent' and deleted the message, no reset link was ever sent, nothing was logged, and P-ACC-07's deliberately identical 202 meant the customer could not tell. On a product where an address is taken permanently and there is no support desk, that is the account gone.

audit_log IS APPEND-ONLY AT THE DATABASE-ROLE LEVEL, NOT BY CONVENTION. The application role holds INSERT and SELECT and no UPDATE and no DELETE. That is a GRANT in the migration, not a column, and S-XCT-07 asserts it by reading information_schema.table_privileges. The merge owner must carry it into the DDL package — a schema that models only columns will silently drop the one control that makes the table evidence.

audit_log's `action` VOCABULARY IS CLOSED AND IS ENFORCED IN PYTHON, NOT IN THE DATABASE. S-ADM-02 requires a closed enum `AuditAction`, S-XCT-07 requires the module-level tuple `AUDIT_ACTIONS` in backend/app/domain/audit.py, and a non-member must be refused at a boundary check BEFORE the transaction opens (asserted by a statement listener recording zero statements). No document asks for a database CHECK or a Postgres enum on this column and I have proposed neither. P-ADM-19's table is the single source of the strings; the one already got wrong is `showtime.base_price_changed` (`showtime.price_changed` is not a member — note that FR-ADR-019's own illustrative text still shows the wrong string).

THE ROLE SET IS FOUR IN CODE AND THREE IN THE COLUMN. S3.1 models guest as 'the absence of a session; not a row', while S-SCP-06 asserts the application Role enum has exactly four members including guest. I have reported the column's values as customer/manager/admin and flagged the divergence rather than resolving it. THE CINEMA-STAFF ROLE IS GONE: SRC-001 §4.3 is withdrawn by erratum E-1 and §5.5.3 by E-3; S-SCP-06 asserts no member name matches staff|usher|door|gate|scanner|attendant and that rg over backend/app and frontend/src for cinema_?staff|door_?scanner|ticket_?validat returns zero hits. There is no scanner, no validation endpoint and no redemption column anywhere in this cluster.

THE 'WHO BOOKED THIS SEAT' REQUIREMENT IS NOT ANSWERED BY audit_log, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. SRC-001 §7.6 asks the question for any seat at any time; P-XCT-04 and S7.3 both answer it from the PERMANENT BOOKING RECORD — (showtime_id, seat_id) -> the seat-occupancy row -> booking_id -> user_id, created_at, and the snapshotted price_paise. A customer booking a seat is 'the product working', not a privileged write, so it writes NO audit row. Three properties make that query total rather than usually-correct and all three land on other clusters: nothing on a path to a booking is ever deleted, booking.user_id is non-null, and the per-seat price is snapshotted at hold acquisition. THE TENSION, STATED: the schema can therefore say who booked a seat but CANNOT say who CHANGED anything about a customer booking, because no customer action is audited at all — and there is no v1 endpoint that changes one, so nothing is currently lost. The moment any customer-initiated mutation is added (cancellation is the obvious one, and `booking.status` and `cancelled_at` already exist in the schema against exactly that day), the audit trail has a hole that P-ADM-19's admin-only vocabulary cannot fill, because it contains no customer action string and forbids any section from coining one. That is a consequence of a rule, not a defect today.

SIGNING IN IS NOT A PRIVILEGED WRITE. P-ACC-02 step 4 writes `last_signed_in_at` in its own implicit transaction with nothing to be atomic with, and inserts NOTHING into audit_log. P-ADM-17 restates it. The column holds only the MOST RECENT sign-in, not a history — a customer signing in on two devices leaves only the later instant, and no source asks for a history.

manager_screen_assignment IS MODELLED HERE BUT ITS `screen_id` BELONGS TO THE VENUE CLUSTER. If the venue reader also modelled it, deduplicate on this version — it carries the audit consequence (the removed row's primary key survives in audit_log.entity_id with no FK) and the explicit zero-check-constraint / zero-trigger assertion that 'two managers per hall' is staffing and not a rule.

NOTHING IN THIS CLUSTER MODELS A HOLD. OPEN-HOLDRECOVER-01 keeps holds in Redis with no table, and none is proposed here. There is no session table either — S-ACC-04 asserts `SELECT to_regclass('session')` returns null, because the JWT is stateless and SRC-002 §7.3 forbids server-side session state. The `pv` claim against `users.password_version` is what makes a stateless session revocable, and it is the only revocation mechanism in the product.

NO CARD DATA AND NO CREDENTIAL EVER REACHES audit_log. `before` and `after` exclude `password_hash` and `password_version` on every entity_type='user' row without exception (P-ADM-17, P-ADM-19), the permitted key set is a subset of {email, role, created_at, last_signed_in_at}, and S-ADM-02 asserts zero rows matching card-shaped keys or JPEG magic bytes. P-XCT-12's central redaction filter covers the log side.

FIVE FIGURES IN THIS CLUSTER ARE CONFIGURATION AND NONE MAY BECOME A LITERAL IN A COLUMN NAME, A COMMENT OR A CONSTRAINT: PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH (12, interpolated into four published strings — a literal 12 in copy is a defect), PASSWORD_RESET_TTL_SECONDS (1800, a [JUDGMENT CALL] — a literal 30 in any customer-visible sentence is a defect), SESSION_TTL_SECONDS (43200, ASSUMED and explicitly never hardening into a constraint), BCRYPT_COST (12, a [JUDGMENT CALL] replaced by Phase 7's measured figure) and RECEIPT_CLAIM_STALE_SECONDS (900). The one number that IS deliberately a literal is bcrypt's 72-byte truncation point, which is a property of the algorithm and has no variable behind it.

TWO ARTICLE X ROWS SIT ON THIS CLUSTER AND NEITHER IS MINE TO CLOSE: OPEN-RESETTOKEN-01 (reserved: secrets) and OPEN-EMAILOWN-01 (reserved: product). OPEN-MGRBOOK-01 (reserved: access control) touches the manager role but is answered by authorisation, not by a column. No column here is shaped to make any of the three cheaper to answer one way, and no plaintext-token column and no address-change column exists.
